task-01-01.instruction: Turn on your recorder and catch a sound that usually slips past your ears. Careful: it might try to escape.

task-01-02.instruction: Record three completely different sounds and introduce them to each other. Will a rustle, a whistle and a fridge become friends?

task-01-03.instruction: Interview any object. If the chair refuses to answer, at least record its suspicious creak.

task-01-04.instruction: Find the most mysterious sound nearby and record it. Don't tell anyone it was the washing machine.

task-02-01.instruction: Record a sound that deserves a thumbs-up: a perfect shot, a beautiful chord or a jar opening just right.

task-02-02.instruction: Get something right on the first try and record the sound of your victory. A happy “yes!” counts as a musical composition too.

task-02-03.instruction: Ask someone to share the kindest news of the day into the microphone. Even “there are still cookies left” will do.

task-02-04.instruction: Record yourself praising a person, an animal or a very hardworking kettle. Make it heartfelt and suitably grand.

task-03-01.instruction: Find the quietest sound in the room and bring the microphone close. Don't scare it off: quiet sounds are very shy.

task-03-02.instruction: Whisper an important secret into the microphone that everyone is allowed to hear. For example: “Pasta tastes better when you aren't looking at it.”

task-03-03.instruction: Walk across the room as quietly as possible and record your mission. If the floor creaks, it's working for the other side.

task-03-04.instruction: Record thirty seconds of almost complete silence. Then listen back and find out who was rustling after all.

task-04-01.instruction: Close your eyes and list all the sounds around you. Record the one hiding furthest away.

task-04-02.instruction: Find a sound you want to hear again and again: purring, rain or a packet of cookies being opened.

task-04-03.instruction: Record an everyday object from very close up, then try to identify it through headphones. No peeking with your ears!

task-04-04.instruction: Make a mini track from three sounds around you. Let the saucepan, keys and cupboard door finally form a band.

task-05-01.instruction: Go for a walk and record three sounds you don't hear at home. A pigeon arguing with a plastic bag gets bonus points.

task-05-02.instruction: Find a sound that lets you recognize your street with your eyes closed, and save it for posterity.

task-05-03.instruction: Record the beginning, middle and end of your walk. You'll have a little film, only you can leave the screen at home.

task-05-04.instruction: Follow the most interesting sound until you find its source. If it's a garbage truck, the expedition is still a success.

task-06-01.instruction: Sit on the grass and record what the leaves are whispering to the wind. No translation from leaf language required.

task-06-02.instruction: Find three sounds of nature and record their performance. An especially loud crow can host the concert.

task-06-03.instruction: Record footsteps on grass, soil and stones. Decide which surface plays the best rustling solo.

task-06-04.instruction: Lie down or sit quietly and record nature without talking. Bird commentary is allowed.

task-07-01.instruction: Listen for the most distant sound around you and go looking for it. Don't go too far if it's the fridge calling.

task-07-02.instruction: Close your eyes, turn on the spot and work out where a sound is coming from. Record the winner of sound hide-and-seek.

task-07-03.instruction: Ask a friend to make a sound behind your back. Record it and try to guess its source without hints or cheating.

task-07-04.instruction: Find a sound whose source you can't see right away. Maybe it's a pipe. Maybe it's a cat. Maybe it's a cat in a pipe.

task-08-01.instruction: Find a moon rock and record its story after returning from another planet. Earth rocks are welcome to audition too.

task-08-02.instruction: Create an alien voice using a glass, a box or an app, and record its first message to Earth.

task-08-03.instruction: Tap different pebbles together and choose the most cosmic sound. Declare it the official voice of the Moon.

task-08-04.instruction: Record a short radio message for astronauts: who you are, where you are and why your other sock has gone missing again.

task-09-01.instruction: Find a repeating sound and dance to it. A car's turn signal can absolutely be a DJ.

task-09-02.instruction: Create a rhythm with claps, footsteps and taps on a table. Record it before the table asks to be paid.

task-09-03.instruction: Play a recording of a sound from your surroundings and invent one signature dance move to go with it.

task-09-04.instruction: Record a sound you can't help moving to. If you can't find one, make your own with two spoons and some enthusiasm.

task-10-01.instruction: Ask a friend to make an unexpected funny sound and record your genuine reaction. Just no air horns right next to your ear.

task-10-02.instruction: Find an object that sounds nothing like it looks. Congratulations: you've discovered a sound in disguise.

task-10-03.instruction: Record a sound that made you turn around. Then give it a grand introduction as the day's greatest discovery.

task-10-04.instruction: Create a sound your friends won't be able to guess. Pasta, a comb and a slipper are officially allowed.

task-11-01.instruction: Play or hum a three-note melody. A fourth note is allowed if it really wants to join in.

task-11-02.instruction: Make a musical sound with a bottle, a straw or rolled-up paper. Probably best not to tell the clarinet about this experiment.

task-11-03.instruction: Give a one-minute concert for a single listener and record the final applause. A stuffed animal counts as a listener.

task-11-04.instruction: Record three different sustained sounds and combine them into one chord. Even a kettle sometimes dreams of playing jazz.

task-12-01.instruction: Find a safe open space and record a long “Hellooo!” Listen for an echo answering back.

task-12-02.instruction: Do the voice of a huge, friendly giant who has lost a tiny spoon. Record the giant's announcement.

task-12-03.instruction: Call a friend with an unusual sound and have them reply with their own. That's how a language no textbook has heard of is born.

task-12-04.instruction: Record a loud sound without shouting into anyone's ear: a clap, a stomp or a thump on a pillow. Look after your hearing and the neighbor's chandelier.

task-13-01.instruction: Record the sounds of your own dance: steps, claps, a jump and a triumphant landing. The furniture isn't part of the act.

task-13-02.instruction: Invent a rhythm that makes your feet start dancing all by themselves, and record twenty seconds of your performance.

task-13-03.instruction: Build a beat from safe kitchen sounds and make your dance-floor entrance. The ladle is today's DJ.

task-13-04.instruction: Ask a friend to invent a movement, then invent a sound for it. Record your choreographed conversation.

task-14-01.instruction: Find the notes that have gone missing in the room and record the sounds of all the suspects. Question the piano especially carefully.

task-14-02.todayLabel: the case of the strange sound
task-14-02.instruction: Record a mysterious noise and ask your friends to guess what made it. You may hide the evidence, but not the slipper.

task-14-03.instruction: Find three sounds that could start a melody. Put them together and declare the case closed.

task-14-04.instruction: Follow a trail of sounds from room to room and record your final discovery. Chances are the culprit is the fridge again.

task-15-01.instruction: Make music with fruit and Playtronica. Record the banana's solo before it starts demanding its own dressing room.

task-15-02.instruction: Record the sounds of a carrot, a cucumber and a lettuce leaf. Don't eat the musicians before the performance is over.

task-15-03.instruction: Build a rhythm from crunches, taps and Playtronica's electronic sounds. The result: a track approved by an imaginary nutritionist.

task-15-04.instruction: Choose a fruit or vegetable and give it a musical personality. An orange might sing opera, while a potato plays hard rock.

task-16-01.instruction: Grab a flashlight and record a sound that only appears in the evening. Rustling pajamas count as nocturnal wildlife too.

task-16-02.instruction: Take a flashlight along a safe route and collect three nighttime sounds. Recording the shadows is optional.

task-16-03.instruction: Tell the microphone what's happening around you after dark. Speak softly: the stars have already gone to bed.

task-16-04.instruction: Record a mysterious nighttime rustle and find out where it comes from. Nine times out of ten it's a bag, but there's still hope.

task-17-01.instruction: Record water, bubbles or gurgling through a straw. Don't suck up your drink in the middle of the grand solo.

task-17-02.instruction: Create the most futuristic sound you can from objects at hand. Name your track as if it were recorded in the year 3026.

task-17-03.instruction: Combine a smooth sound, a round sound and a hissing sound in one recording. Imagine it's the soundtrack for a dancing jellyfish.

task-17-04.instruction: Record a voice message from a world where sounds are visible as bubbles. Tell us what color your “boom” is today.

task-18-01.instruction: Record dribbling a ball, a kick and a happy shout after a goal. If you miss, it was an experimental pass.

task-18-02.instruction: Invent a short chant for your team and record it together. Your team can be just you and one ball.

task-18-03.instruction: Record a ball on three different surfaces. Let the grass, asphalt and floor compete for the best bass.

task-18-04.instruction: Narrate a football moment like a real commentator. The more dramatically you say “ball,” the better.

task-19-01.instruction: Find a friend and record your happiest greeting. Wings and a banana costume are optional, but welcome.

task-19-02.instruction: Invent a voice for a winged banana and record it inviting everyone to fly. Include the rules for bringing peels on board.

task-19-03.instruction: Ask a friend which sound reminds them of you. Try not to be offended if it's the crunch of chips.

task-19-04.instruction: Hug someone close to you or your favorite toy and record the sound of the moment. Sometimes a hug sounds like “oof.”

task-20-01.instruction: Record a skateboard rolling along a smooth surface. A helmet is required; a superhero facial expression is optional.

task-20-02.instruction: Build a beat from wheels, footsteps and a safe tap on the board. The city is ready to dance.

task-20-03.instruction: Record a simple, safe skateboard move and the audience's grand reaction. Even one spectator is enough.

task-20-04.instruction: Compare the sounds of a skateboard, a scooter and a toy car. Hold a race where the most interesting noise wins.
